messages:
Ana: FYI from the cloud marketplace call  partners want a single coherent billing waterfall that shows how commit discounts, co-sell credits, SI payments, and any appliance fees apply over Y1 and renewal. Need a canonical example.
Ben: We should show an order-of-operations waterfall: 1) apply commit discount to platform list, 2) add appliance surcharge (if selected), 3) apply smoothing credits (vested), 4) apply co-sell cashouts to partner invoices. Makes it obvious to procurement.
Kofi: Suggest we introduce a "staged churn protection" mechanism instead of refunds: if trailing 3mo usage < X% customer gets a staged remediation package (extend term 2-3 months + apply up to Y% of vested credits). Keeps cash in platform and avoids refund accounting headaches.
Lily: Good call. Also partners asked whether SI success payments reduce the committed spend. Short answer: no. SI payments are separate and can be used to offset invoices if customer and Redwood opt in, but they do not count toward the commit math. Call this out clearly.
Ana: Draft example (compact):
````
Commit = $600k/yr
1) 18% commit discount -> discounted commit = $492k
2) Appliance surcharge (if any) +5% -> +$24.6k -> subtotal 516.6k
3) Vested smoothing credits (total $30k, $5k/mo) applied to invoices if customer elects remediation or applied to SI invoice per agreement
4) Co-sell credit payout (partner) processed separately after joint milestone; does not reduce recognized ARR
Net effect shown in timeline: what gets invoiced vs what is reserved as credits.
````
Ben: Procurement language: avoid "refund". Use "applied credits" or "term extension". Also require a written remediation plan to unlock any application of smoothing credits.
Kofi: Ops: add a meter parity tolerance of 2% in first billing cycle post-listing. If divergence >2%, open an immediate reconciliation and pause credit vesting until fixed. Keeps disputes low.
Lily: For co-marketing/co-sell stacking: default = no stacking with public promos. If partner wants stacking, require explicit RevOps sign-off and list the stacking in the private-offer attachment so marketplace UI shows it.
Ana: Announcement cadence: don't list private-offer until SI toolkit and partner marketing assets are ready. Recommend joint customer-facing announcement 7 days after close and marketplace listing 14 days after close.
Ben: Finance note to include in playbook: smoothing credits are deferred and recognized when consumed; co-sell cashouts are expense items and do not change ARR recognition. We'll include a one-line note for RevOps.
Kofi: Contract clause draft: "Staged Churn Protection: If trailing 3-month average usage falls below 65%, customer may elect (i) a 3-month term extension OR (ii) apply up to 40% of remaining vested smoothing credits as invoice credit; both subject to signed remediation plan and CSM sign-off."
Lily: SKU naming guidance: keep listing title short: "Redwood Commit (PrivOffer) - 1Y - BandX" and attach a 1-pager PDF with waterfall math, SKU mappings, meter IDs, reconciliation cadence.
Ana: Action items: Ben -> sample waterfall spreadsheet + three scenarios (fast ramp, slow ramp, appliance). Kofi -> reconciliation spec + meter tolerance enforcement. Lily -> private-offer attachment template + FAQ for procurement. I'll collate and share draft by Thu EOD.
partner-bot: Task created: waterfall-playbook-staged-churn -> owner: Ana, due_in: 3 business days (task id: WP-4441).
Ben: I'll ping Legal + RevOps for wording. Quick Q: floor discount we want public?
Ana: Floor = 4% without CRO approval. Call it out in the playbook.
Kofi: :thumbsup:
Lily: :thumbsup:
Ana: Thanks team, small thread but should give procurement what they need.
